title: The wake: family, red beans, drink and lodge suppers
summary: Families laid out the dead at home and fed visitors red beans and rice, beer, wine and coffee all night. Rene mentions society suppers.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, when somebody was laid out, who would be there with the body?

The family? Well, they used to lay them out in the house. They used to lay them out in the house. See, the family would be there. And they'd have work all night. Some of them used to have spaghettas. I used to look for them kind of, quick. The last week I made it right here on, on Saratoga between Washington and 6th. They had a red bean breakfast. They said, I had red bean. I stood all night waiting for that red bean. Boy, it was good too. They had ham, bone, everything. It was trouble. But they don't do that anymore. All that doesn't pass. Everything go to Undertaker, 12 o'clock, they put you out.
What would they have with the red beans?
Oh yeah, they had beer too. They had beer and wine. Eh?
The family. The family would fix the food. The family would cook the food.
They'd drink a little beer and wine and coffee?

Oh yeah, they'd be drinking that all night. They'd be drinking it. They'd be, you know. They got a, I don't even forgot, I believe the stand handlers, I believe them gives a supper when they die. I don't know. I heard. But there's some one of them clubs or some one of them unions, they have a supper. They have supper. Every time they have a week, they have supper. You heard of that?

Yeah, well they used to have a supper. I'm going to find out. I'll let you all know who he was. But I think it was the stand handlers out in front of the town. Because I was supposed to go up and they were supposed to have chicken and spaghetti. Italian cheese. One time. That's right, he'd give supper.
